examples.en: Have you tried red bean bread in Korea?
I had red bean bread and milk for breakfast.
This bakery is most famous for its red bean bread.

examples.ko: 이 팥빵 안에는 팥이 가득 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This red bean bread is full of red bean filling.
My grandmother likes warm red bean bread.

examples.ko: 팥빵 두 개랑 커피 한 잔 주세요.
examples.en: Two red bean breads and a cup of coffee, please.

explain: '단팥빵'이라고도 해요. 빵 이름은 '팥'처럼 속 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여서 '크림빵', '소보로빵'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Two sweet red bean buns, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: '팥빵'과 같은 빵이고, 빵집 이름표에는 이 말이 더 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same bun as 'patppang', and more common on bakery labels.

phrases.en: I like cream bread more than red bean bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속 재료 이름을 붙인 다른 빵이에요. 비교할 때 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another bread named for its filling, often compared with it.

phrases.en: I bought a red bean bun at the bakery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팥빵을 어디서 사는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where you buy it.
phrases.en_equiv: to buy red bean bread at a bakery

explain_en: It is also called '단팥빵'. Korean bread names often put the filling or topping first, like '크림빵' (cream bread) and '소보로빵' (streusel bread).

examples.en: I make stew with sour kimchi.
I stir-fried sour kimchi and ate it with rice.
There is one head of sour kimchi left in the fridge.

examples.ko: 이 김치는 푹 익어서 신김치가 됐어요.
examples.en: This kimchi fermented well and has turned sour.
Dumplings with sour kimchi are tangy and tasty.
My mother made me pancakes with sour kimchi.

explain: 푹 익어서 시큼해진 김치예요. 그대로 먹기보다 찌개, 볶음, 전, 만두처럼 요리에 넣을 때가 많아요. 갓 담근 김치는 '겉절이'라고 해서 맛이 달라요.

phrases.en: I make stew with aged kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 익힌 김치예요. '신김치'보다 깊은 맛이 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Kimchi aged for a long time, with a deeper flavor feel than 'singimchi'.

phrases.en: I made kimchi stew with sour kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신김치로 가장 많이 만드는 대표 요리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical dish made with sour kimchi.

phrases.en: I make kimchi fried rice with sour kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신김치를 볶아서 밥과 함께 먹는 간단한 요리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple dish of stir-fried sour kimchi with rice.

explain_en: This is kimchi that has fermented a lot and become sour. It is often used in cooking, such as stew, stir-fries, pancakes and dumplings, rather than eaten as is. Freshly made kimchi is called '겉절이' and tastes different.

examples.en: On rainy days we eat seafood scallion pancake.
One seafood scallion pancake here, please.
This place's seafood scallion pancake is crispy outside.
Yesterday my grandmother fried a seafood scallion pancake for me.
It's a seafood scallion pancake full of squid and shrimp.
I dip seafood scallion pancake in soy sauce.

explain: 파만 넣은 것은 '파전'이고, 오징어나 새우 같은 해물이 들어가면 '해물파전'이에요. 만들 때는 '부치다'를 쓰고, 세는 단위는 '한 장'이에요. 한국에서는 비 오는 날 파전을 많이 찾는다고 해요.

phrases.en: I like scallion pancakes without seafood too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해물파전'에서 해물이 빠진 것으로, 파만 넣고 부친 전이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The version without seafood, made with just scallions.

phrases.example: 여기 해물파전 한 장 더 주세요.
phrases.en: One more seafood scallion pancake here, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주문할 때 쓰는 말로, 해물파전은 '한 장'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering at a restaurant; this pancake is counted with the unit for flat sheets.

phrases.en: It's raining, so my mom is frying seafood scallion pancakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만들다'보다 기름에 얇게 굽는 요리를 말할 때 '부치다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The cooking verb for pan-frying something thin in oil, more specific than just saying 'make'.

explain_en: One with only scallions is '파전', and with seafood such as squid or shrimp it is '해물파전'. The verb for making it is '부치다', and the counter is '한 장'. In Korea, people are said to crave pajeon on rainy days.

examples.en: I'm eating hot pot with my family this evening.
It's cold, so I think of hot, steaming hot pot.

examples.ko: 훠궈 집에서 매운 마라 육수를 골랐어요.
examples.en: At the hot pot place, I chose the spicy mala broth.
I bought vegetables to put in the hot pot at the mart.

examples.ko: 저는 매운 육수보다 맑은 훠궈가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like clear hot pot more than spicy broth.
We chatted while eating hot pot with friends.

explain: 훠궈는 중국식 전골 요리로, 끓는 육수에 재료를 직접 담가 익혀 먹어요. 한국 사람들은 '마라탕', '샤브샤브'와 비교해서 말하기도 해요. 중국어에서 온 말이라서 '훠궈 집', '훠궈 육수'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 동네에 새 훠궈 집이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: A new hot pot restaurant opened in our neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훠궈를 파는 식당을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A restaurant that serves hot pot.

phrases.en: The hot pot broth is very spicy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훠궈 국물을 말해요. 안 매운 것도 있고 매운 것도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The soup base of hot pot; some kinds are mild and some are spicy.

phrases.en: On cold days, I want to eat hot pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 먹는다고 말할 때 가장 기본으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic way to say you eat hot pot.

explain_en: Hot pot is a Chinese-style dish where you cook ingredients yourself in boiling broth. Koreans often compare it with '마라탕' and '샤브샤브'. It comes from Chinese, and you can use it in phrases like '훠궈 집' and '훠궈 육수'.

examples.ko: 저는 여름에 체리를 제일 많이 먹어요.
examples.en: I eat cherries the most in summer.

examples.ko: 케이크 위에 빨간 체리가 올라가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a red cherry on top of the cake.
I bought a box of cherries at the mart.
These cherries are sweet and very fresh.

examples.ko: 여기 체리 주스 한 잔 주세요.
examples.en: One glass of cherry juice, please.

examples.ko: 동생은 과일 중에서 체리만 골라 먹어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling picks out only the cherries from the fruit.

explain: '체리'는 서양에서 온 열매 이름이고, 한국에서 옛날부터 먹던 작고 빨간 '앵두'는 다른 과일이에요. 과일 이름이라서 '체리 주스', '체리 케이크'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I'll have the cherry juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카페나 식당에서 음료를 주문할 때 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Handy for ordering a drink at a cafe or restaurant.

phrases.en: I ate cherry cake on my birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 이름 앞에 '체리'를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the fruit name before a food to name it.

phrases.en: This candy is cherry flavored.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과자나 사탕의 맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the flavor of snacks or candy.

explain_en: '체리' is the name of the Western fruit. The small red '앵두', which Koreans have eaten for a long time, is a different fruit. It often goes in front of other words, as in '체리 주스' and '체리 케이크'.

examples.en: I put a little basil in the pasta this evening.
I grow basil on our balcony.
This basil smells really good.
Tomatoes and basil go really well together.

examples.ko: 피자 위에 신선한 바질 잎을 올렸어요.
examples.en: I put fresh basil leaves on the pizza.
I spread basil sauce on bread and eat it.

explain: 파스타, 피자, 토마토 요리에 많이 쓰는 허브예요. 잎은 '바질 잎', 가루는 '바질 가루', 소스는 '바질 페스토'처럼 말해요. 집에서 '바질을 키우다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I put basil leaves on top of the pizza.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신선한 잎을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the fresh leaves.

phrases.en: I spread basil pesto on bread and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바질로 만든 소스를 말해요. 파스타에도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sauce made from basil, often used with pasta.

phrases.en: I grow basil by the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 식물로 기를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you grow the plant at home.

explain_en: It is an herb widely used in pasta, pizza, and tomato dishes. People say '바질 잎' for the leaf, '바질 가루' for the powder, and '바질 페스토' for the sauce. You can also say '바질을 키우다' for growing it at home.

examples.en: Wow, this tteokbokki looks really delicious.
It looks delicious just from the photo!
That cake looks delicious. Where did you buy it?
I smell stew. It must be really tasty.
The meat is cooked golden brown, so it looks delicious.

examples.ko: 그 가게 빵은 다 맛있겠어요. 뭘 살까요?
examples.en: All the bread in that shop looks delicious. What should we buy?

explain: 먹기 전에 보거나 냄새를 맡고 느낌을 말할 때 써요. 먹은 뒤에는 '맛있어요/맛있었어요'라고 해요. 친구에게는 '맛있겠다'나 '맛있겠네'라고 하고, '맛있어 보여요'도 비슷해요.

phrases.en: Wow, this cake looks delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가까운 사람에게 하는 반말이에요. 감탄하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech to friends, with a tone of admiration.

phrases.en: This gimbap looks tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈으로 본 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when judging by how it looks.

phrases.en: Looking at the photo, I want to eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛있어 보여서 먹고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you want to eat it because it looks good.

explain_en: Use it when you react to food before eating it, by seeing or smelling it. After eating, say '맛있어요/맛있었어요'. To friends you'd say '맛있겠다' or '맛있겠네', and '맛있어 보여요' is similar.

examples.en: This food is strongly seasoned for me.

examples.ko: 국이 간이 세서 물을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: The soup was too strongly seasoned, so I added more water.

examples.ko: 할머니 음식은 조금 간이 센 편이에요.
examples.en: My grandmother's food is a bit strongly seasoned.

examples.ko: 간이 세면 밥을 많이 먹게 돼요.
examples.en: When it's strongly seasoned, you end up eating a lot of rice.

examples.ko: 이 김치찌개는 간이 너무 세지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't this kimchi stew too strongly seasoned?

examples.ko: 아이 음식은 간이 세지 않게 만들어요.
examples.en: I make the children's food not too strongly seasoned.

explain: '간'은 음식의 짠 정도를 말해요. 반대는 '간이 싱겁다'이고, 알맞으면 '간이 맞다'라고 해요. 맛을 보며 짠 정도를 확인하는 건 '간을 보다'예요. 몸의 '간(liver)'과는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: This soup is too salty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '간이 세다'보다 짧고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter and more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The soup was bland, so I added salt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '간이 세다'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite expression.

phrases.en: This stew is seasoned just right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짜지도 싱겁지도 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is neither too salty nor too bland.

explain_en: '간' refers to how salty the seasoning of food is. The opposite is '간이 싱겁다', and when it is just right you say '간이 맞다'. Tasting to check the saltiness is '간을 보다'. It only sounds the same as the liver, but it is a different word.

examples.en: The food prices at this restaurant are really cheap.
Let's each pay for our own food today.

examples.ko: 우리는 모임이 끝나고 음식값을 따로따로 계산했어요.
examples.en: After the gathering, we paid for our food separately.
Food prices have gone up a lot lately, so it's a burden.

examples.ko: 음식값이 너무 비싸서 다른 곳으로 갔어요.
examples.en: The food was too expensive, so we went somewhere else.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 음식값도 싸고 양도 많아요.
examples.en: This shop has cheap prices and big portions too.

explain: 식당에서 먹은 음식의 값을 말해요. 대화에서는 '밥값'도 자주 써요. 한 달 동안 음식에 쓰는 돈은 '식비'라고 해서 서로 달라요.

phrases.en: I'll pay for the meal today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 '음식값'보다 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in conversation than the formal word.

phrases.en: My friend paid for the food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹은 음식의 돈을 계산한다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to say you pay for the food you ate.

phrases.example: 저는 한 달 식비가 많이 나와요.
phrases.en: My monthly food costs are high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 달 동안 음식에 쓰는 돈 전체를 말해요. 한 끼 값과 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: The total money spent on food over a period, not the price of one meal.

explain_en: It means the price of food eaten at a restaurant. In conversation people also often say '밥값'. The money you spend on food over a month is '식비', which is a different word.

examples.ko: 넓이를 말할 때는 제곱미터라는 단위를 써요.
examples.en: When talking about area, we use the unit 'square meter'.
In Korea, weight is measured in kilograms.
Korea's unit of money is the won.

examples.ko: 이 달걀은 열 개 단위로 팔아요.
examples.en: These eggs are sold in tens.

examples.ko: 시간 단위로 돈을 받는 아르바이트가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many part-time jobs where you're paid by the hour.

explain: ‘~ 단위로’는 ‘~씩 묶어서’라는 뜻으로 자주 써요. 예를 들어 ‘일 년 단위로 계약해요’는 일 년씩 계약한다는 말이에요.
explain_en: ~ 단위로 is often used to mean “in blocks of ~.” For example, 일 년 단위로 계약해요 means you sign a contract one year at a time.

examples.en: It rained a lot yesterday.
I walked a lot today.
I drink a lot of water.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 점심에 사람이 많이 와요.
examples.en: A lot of people come to this restaurant at lunchtime.
I met a lot of friends in Korea.

explain: ‘많이’는 동사 앞에 와요: 많이 먹어요. 명사 뒤에는 ‘많아요’를 써요: 사람이 많아요. 둘을 같이 쓰면 ‘사람이 많이 와요’가 돼요.

dict_examples.en: It snowed a lot overnight.

explain_en: 많이 goes before a verb (많이 먹어요). After a noun use 많아요 (사람이 많아요). Put together you get 사람이 많이 와요.

examples.en: On rainy days I think of pajeon.
I dip pajeon in spicy soy sauce.
On the weekend my mom pan-fried pajeon for me.
Excuse me, one seafood pajeon, please.

examples.ko: 프라이팬 위에서 파전이 노릇노릇 익고 있어요.
examples.en: The pajeon is cooking golden brown in the frying pan.

examples.ko: 파전 반죽에 오징어를 넣으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes better if you put squid in the pajeon batter.

explain: '부침개'는 기름에 부친 음식 전체이고, 파전은 그중 파가 들어간 것이에요. 동사는 '부치다'를 써서 '파전을 부치다'라고 해요. '붙이다'와 헷갈리지 마세요. 한국 사람들은 비 오는 날 기름 소리가 빗소리 같아서 파전을 먹는다고 말해요.
explain_en: 'Buchimgae' is the general word for pan-fried batter dishes, and pajeon is the kind with green onions. The verb is '부치다' (pan-fry), as in '파전을 부치다', not '붙이다' (stick). Koreans often say they crave pajeon on rainy days because the sizzling sounds like rain.

examples.en: Grandma is coming down from the second floor.
After coming down the mountain, we had some makgeolli.
The elevator didn't come, so I came down the stairs.
Please come down for a moment. A package has arrived.
My friend came down from Seoul to Busan.

explain: 내가 아래에 있으면 “내려와요”, 내가 위에 있으면 “내려가요”예요. 말하는 사람이 기준이에요.

phrases.en: to be handed down (from generation to generation)
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날부터 이어져 와요
phrases.nuance_en: used for stories or customs that have been passed on since long ago
phrases.en_equiv: to be handed down (from generation to generation)

dict_examples.en: The children, perhaps tired, rested several times as they came down the road.

explain_en: For height, Koreans say 크다/작다 (big/small), never 높다 (high). In Korea people talk about height quite openly, even with someone they just met.

p.n: 키 is for people and plants; 높이 fits any object.

usage: 셋 = three (counting). Before a counter: 세 개.

examples.en: My younger sibling counts one, two, three.
There are three of us in my family.
Three books, please.
Three americanos, please.
Three dumplings, please.

explain: '셋'은 세는 말 앞에서 '세'로 바뀌어요: 세 개, 세 시, 세 명. 혼자 쓸 때는 그대로 '셋'이에요(친구 셋이 왔어요). '달' 앞에서는 '석 달'이라고도 해요.

explain_en: '셋' becomes 세 before a counter: 세 개 (three things), 세 시 (three o'clock), 세 명 (three people). On its own it stays 셋 (친구 셋이 왔어요, three friends came). Before 달 (months) you will also hear 석 달.
